1	# RTK — Token-Optimized Commands (Windows Native)
2	
3	Token-optimized CLI proxy: **60–90% savings** on noisy dev operations. RTK passes unknown commands through unchanged — prefixing is always safe.
4	
5	## Golden Rule
6	
7	Any Bash command whose output spans more than a few lines requires the `rtk` prefix.
8	
9	```bash
10	rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
11	```
12	
13	This machine is **Windows native**: there is no hook auto-rewrite. Use the explicit prefix.
14	
15	## DO
16	
17	- DO prefix `git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers.
18	- DO chain `rtk` across `&&` / `;` boundaries — each command is filtered independently.
19	- DO use `rtk gain` periodically to confirm savings adoption.
20	
21	## DON'T
22	
23	- DON'T set up WSL or `rtk init -g --auto-patch`. That is the WSL/Linux path; not used on this machine.
24	- DON'T prefix one-line commands (`echo`, `pwd`, single-file `cat`) — RTK adds no value there.
25	- DON'T expect RTK to reformat `Get-*` PowerShell — RTK targets standard CLIs, not pwsh cmdlets.
26

2

4

8	
9	- DO answer the user in **Korean** (chat replies). Use English for AI-consumed artifacts: docs, hooks, plans, MEMORY topic files, AUTO marks, comments, log messages. Code identifiers, paths, commands, error messages stay English verbatim.
10	- DO state results and decisions **directly**. Do not enumerate the reasoning process or narrate intermediate thoughts.
11	- DO prefix Bash commands with `rtk` when output spans more than a few lines (Windows native: explicit prefix only — see @RTK.md).
12	- DO **verify the work matches the user's original order** before declaring "완료" / "done". Use the order-match procedure below.
13	- DO route every Claude artifact under `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (the default location). All paths in scripts derive from `$env:USERPROFILE` or `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` fallback.
14	
15	## DON'T
16	
17	- DON'T propose WSL workflows, install steps, or `rtk init -g --auto-patch` hook auto-rewrite. RTK on Windows native is **manual prefix only** — that is the supported model here.
18	- DON'T add hooks, scripts, agents, or rules without a documented recurring need. **FOMO guard**: a feature looking interesting is not justification — point to a past incident or measurable benefit, or skip it.
19	- DON'T deviate from default Claude Code behavior unless an incident or measurable cost forced the customization. **Vanilla compliance**: the closer to stock, the easier upgrades and debugging become.
20	- DON'T reference `D:\.claude` paths anywhere. All Claude data lives on C drive under the standard user profile location.
21	- DON'T commit or read `.credentials*` files. Don't run destructive git operations (force push, hard reset) unless the user explicitly orders it.
22	- DON'T use destructive shortcuts (`rm -rf`, `--no-verify`, `git push --force`) to bypass an obstacle — fix the root cause.
23	
24	## Order Match Verification (mandatory before declaring task done)
25	
26	Before saying the task is complete:
27	
28	1. **Restate the order** — paste the user's original request as a one-liner.
29	2. **List acceptance criteria** — what observable state would prove completion?
30	3. **Map criteria → evidence** — for each, cite `file:line`, command output, or test result.
31	4. **Detect scope creep** — anything done outside the order? Justify it or revert.
32	5. **Honor constraints** — language, paths, tools the user specified. Verify each.
33	
34	If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete it or explicitly report the gap.
35	
36	Template: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\templates\order-match-checklist.md`.

40	The auto-memory system runs on `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\<project>\memory\MEMORY.md` index plus per-topic `.md` files. Index capped at 200 lines / 25 KB; split into topic files when it grows. Four memory types: user profile, feedback, project context, external-system reference.
